title: The World Is Yours / Ahmad Jamal
hook: The World Is Yours started as Ahmad Jamal, 1970.
voiceover: The World Is Yours started as Ahmad Jamal, 1970. Ahmad Jamal is a Pittsburgh jazz pianist. In 1970 he put out an album on Impulse called The Awakening. Track 2 is I Love Music. A couple of minutes in there's a piano figure that just floats. 24 years later Pete Rock took that figure for Nas on Illmatic. He didn't loop the whole phrase. He grabbed the chords, ran them under his own drums and bassline, and sang the hook himself. Whose world is this. Same piano, different life, and Ahmad Jamal was still touring while it played on every corner. Save this before you go pull The Awakening. Which flip do you want Monday?
caption: The World Is Yours (Nas, Illmatic, Columbia, 1994, produced by Pete Rock) is built on I Love Music from Ahmad Jamal's The Awakening (Impulse!, 1970). Pete Rock took the piano chords, put his own drums under them, and sang the hook himself. The Awakening is one of the most sampled jazz records of the 70s; this is the flip that made me buy it. Which one should I break down Monday?
